<hypothesis>
**Hypothesis discrimination**: The next key distinction is between catalyst activation (M6, M8) and product inhibition (M12, M17, M18). Catalyst activation mechanisms predict a lag phase before turnover, while product inhibition mechanisms predict immediate suppression of turnover frequency.

**Discriminative experiment design**: A low substrate concentration (0.5 M) with fixed [cat]=0.05 and [P]=0.5 will stress the system. If catalyst activation is required (M6, M8), the rate will be even lower due to limited substrate to drive activation. Product inhibition mechanisms will show reduced but consistent turnover without a lag phase.

**Contrastive prediction**: 
- For M6/M8 (catalyst activation): Initial rate will be significantly lower due to slow cat→cat* conversion (rate ∝ [cat*] instead of [cat]).
- For M12/M17/M18 (product inhibition): Initial rate will decrease proportionally to [S] (rate ∝ [S][cat] initially, but suppressed by [P]).
- For M1/M10/M15 (no activation/inhibition): Rate will follow baseline behavior (rate ∝ [S][cat] initially).
</hypothesis>
